featured_techniques.technique: Brake fluid level check, visual leak inspection around master cylinder and booster
Identifying sealed cooling system with pressure cap and cautions for hot systems
Air intake inspection and locating the air filter housing with MAF sensor awareness
Oil dipstick procedure and reading oil level with max/min marks
Transmission fluid check with engine running and contaminant assessment
Battery inspection: corrosion signs, hold-down, and terminal security

sections.description: Describe where the hood latch is found (left kick panel or under the steering column) and the need to lift the hood safely, noting that some vehicles have pistons that can drop if not secured.
sections.title: Hood release and initial safety

sections.description: Identify the brake master cylinder on the left side, with the booster attached; introduce the idea that braking assist is provided by the booster and that fluid sits in the reservoir on the opposite side of the firewall.
sections.title: Brake system orientation and brake master cylinder

sections.description: Explain how to check brake fluid level, note a very low level, and describe common reasons (worn brake pads or leaks). Describe visual cues for leaks around the master cylinder and booster and explain why leaks are a safety concern.
sections.title: Brake fluid level and leakage indicators

sections.description: Introduce the radiator/cap area and discuss the difference between open caps and sealed systems. Explain the recommended pressure (16 psi for this vehicle) and how a pressure tester would be used; describe symptoms of a failing cap (odor or white crusts) and note other potential leak points in the cooling system.
sections.title: Coolant system basics and pressure cap

sections.description: Differentiate electrical fans from mechanical fans with a clutch and explain when each type operates to cool the engine.
sections.title: Cooling fan types and operation

sections.description: Demonstrate opening the air filter housing, inspecting a relatively new filter, and noting that a dirty filter causes restricted airflow; highlight securing the air filter housing to prevent unfiltered air from entering. Briefly reference the MAF sensor location and cleanliness.
sections.title: Air intake and air filter inspection

sections.description: Show the reservoir path to the pump, advise turning the vehicle off before checking, and describe looking at fluid level and condition; mention that air in the system can cause wind noise when idling or accelerating.
sections.title: Power steering basics

sections.description: Identify the oil fill cap location on the valve cover, read the oil grade (example 5W-20), and describe using the dipstick to assess level between maximum and minimum marks; discuss winter/summer differences and safe ranges, including hot vs cold expansion.
sections.title: Engine oil dipstick check and oil grade

sections.description: Explain checking the transmission fluid with the engine running on a level surface, inspecting color consistency (red vs other colors) to detect contaminants, and rechecking after wiping and reinserting the dipstick.
sections.title: Transmission fluid check and interpretation

sections.description: Note that some manual transmissions share brake fluid in the clutch master cylinder; identify DOT 3 as common for clutches. Describe checking washer fluid and variations in color, reinforcing windshield visibility importance.
sections.title: Clutch fluid and washer fluid basics

sections.description: Cover battery health and typical three-to-five-year lifespan, signs of terminal corrosion, and the need for a secure hold-down. Mention that the engine computer may be under the hood or in the cabin, and that a fuse box is present with fuses/relays.
sections.title: Battery, ECU, fuse box and electrical systems basics

sections.description: Differentiate vehicles with a separate ignition coil from those with a direct coil over plugs, and describe distributor caps with wires leading to spark plugs located on various positions on the engine.
sections.title: Ignition system components

sections.description: Explain the alternator’s role in charging the battery, show the serpentine belt and its pulleys, and warn about belts with missing grooves or misalignment that can cause damage.
sections.title: Alternator and serpentine belt

sections.description: Mention condensation from AC lines as normal when AC is running, and describe how external temperatures can create visible moisture beneath the vehicle.
sections.title: AC condensation notes

sections.description: Summarize the essentials—focus on battery condition and fluid levels—and encourage referencing the owner's manual and maintaining a maintenance schedule for reliability.
sections.title: Wrap-up and maintenance reminders

summary: In this instructional overview, Len from 1A Auto guides viewers through fundamental under-the-hood checks and considerations. The video emphasizes using the owner's manual as a starting point, then details practical checks and observations across several systems: locating the hood release and safety concerns, brake master cylinder and fluid level with leak indicators, coolant/pressure-cap considerations in a sealed cooling system, and cooling fan types. It also covers the air intake path and mass airflow sensor visibility, power steering fluid levels, engine oil dipstick technique and oil grade, transmission fluid checks, washer fluid basics, battery condition and terminal health, engine computer/fuse box awareness, ignition components, alternator and serpentine belt condition, and AC condensation. Throughout, the host underscores safety (not opening hot caps) and maintenance habits (referencing the owner’s manual and a regular maintenance schedule).
title: Under the Hood Basics: Core Fluid, Electrical, and Component Checks
